title: OSHA construction electrical safety practice questions
description: Free OSHA construction electrical safety practice questions. Every answer is explained and linked to the section of 29 CFR 1926 Subpart K it comes from.

questions.question: Where must the written description of an assured equipment grounding conductor program be available?

options.A: At the jobsite, for inspection and copying by the Assistant Secretary and any affected employee
options.B: At the employer's head office only
options.C: On file with the local building department
options.D: Nowhere; the program does not need to be written

questions.explanation: "A written description of the program, including the specific procedures adopted by the employer, shall be available at the jobsite for inspection and copying by the Assistant Secretary and any affected employee."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.404, Wiring design and protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Receptacles on a two-wire, single-phase portable or vehicle-mounted generator need no GFCI if the generator's circuit conductors are insulated from its frame and all other grounded surfaces and the generator is rated at no more than how much?

options.A: 10kW
options.B: 5kW
options.C: 25kW
options.D: 50kW

questions.explanation: The exception covers a generator "rated not more than 5kW, where the circuit conductors of the generator are insulated from the generator frame and all other grounded surfaces."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.404, Wiring design and protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under an assured equipment grounding conductor program, by what means may the required test record be kept?

options.A: Only in a notarized paper ledger
options.B: Only by a stamp on each tool
options.C: By means of logs, color coding, or other effective means
options.D: No record is required

questions.explanation: "Tests performed as required in this paragraph shall be recorded." The record "shall be kept by means of logs, color coding, or other effective means."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.404, Wiring design and protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under an assured equipment grounding conductor program, a cord set has not met the program's requirements. What does the rule say about it?

options.A: It may be used for one more day
options.B: It may be used outdoors only
options.C: It may be used once its plug is taped
options.D: The employer shall not make it available or permit its use by employees

questions.explanation: "The employer shall not make available or permit the use by employees of any equipment which has not met the requirements of this paragraph (b)(1)(iii) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.404, Wiring design and protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under an assured equipment grounding conductor program, which test must be done on all equipment grounding conductors?

options.A: A test for continuity; they shall be electrically continuous
options.B: A 1,000-volt insulation resistance test
options.C: A voltage drop test under full load
options.D: An arc flash test

questions.explanation: "All equipment grounding conductors shall be tested for continuity and shall be electrically continuous."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.404, Wiring design and protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under an assured equipment grounding conductor program, what is the longest interval the rule allows between tests of cord sets and receptacles that are fixed and not exposed to damage?

options.A: 12 months
options.B: 6 months
options.C: 5 years
options.D: 10 years

questions.explanation: The rule says "cord sets and receptacles which are fixed and not exposed to damage shall be tested at intervals not exceeding 6 months."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.404, Wiring design and protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: To protect employees on construction sites against ground faults, which choice does 1926.404(b)(1) give the employer?

options.A: Using double-insulated tools in place of any other protection
options.B: Placing rubber mats at each work station
options.C: Ground-fault circuit interrupters as specified, or an assured equipment grounding conductor program
options.D: Any grounding method the electrician prefers

questions.explanation: "The employer shall use either ground fault circuit interrupters as specified in paragraph (b)(1)(ii) of this section or an assured equipment grounding conductor program as specified in paragraph (b)(1)(iii) of this section to protect employees on construction sites."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.404, Wiring design and protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Portable electric lighting used inside a tank (a wet or conductive location) without GFCI protection must operate at what voltage?

options.A: 240 volts or less
options.B: 120 volts or less
options.C: 48 volts or less
options.D: 12 volts or less

questions.explanation: Such lighting "shall be operated at 12 volts or less. However, 120-volt lights may be used if protected by a ground-fault circuit interrupter."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.405, Wiring methods, components, and equipment for general use (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When may temporary lights be suspended by their electric cords?

options.A: Only when the cords and lights are designed for this means of suspension
options.B: Whenever the light weighs less than 5 pounds
options.C: Whenever the cord is wrapped in tape
options.D: Whenever the lights are used indoors

questions.explanation: "Temporary lights shall not be suspended by their electric cords unless cords and lights are designed for this means of suspension."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.405, Wiring methods, components, and equipment for general use (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When must temporary wiring be removed?

options.A: Within one year of installation
options.B: Immediately upon completion of construction or the purpose for which it was installed
options.C: Only when the building owner asks
options.D: At the end of each work week

questions.explanation: "Temporary wiring shall be removed immediately upon completion of construction or the purpose for which the wiring was installed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.405, Wiring methods, components, and equipment for general use (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In temporary wiring, where does the rule forbid branch-circuit conductors to be laid?

options.A: In raceways
options.B: Inside multiconductor cable assemblies
options.C: On the floor
options.D: On insulators

questions.explanation: The rule states: "No branch-circuit conductors shall be laid on the floor." Runs of open conductors must also be located where they will not be subject to physical damage.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.405, Wiring methods, components, and equipment for general use (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When may flexible cords and cables pass through doorways or other pinch points?

options.A: Never, under any condition
options.B: Only when the cord is unplugged
options.C: Only if the cord is designed for extra-hard usage
options.D: If protection is provided to avoid damage

questions.explanation: "Flexible cords and cables may pass through doorways or other pinch points, if protection is provided to avoid damage."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.405, Wiring methods, components, and equipment for general use (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How must flexible cords be connected to devices and fittings?

options.A: So that strain relief prevents pull from being directly transmitted to joints or terminal screws
options.B: With the outer jacket stripped back past the clamp
options.C: With the conductors twisted together without a fitting
options.D: Loosely, so the cord pulls free under strain

questions.explanation: "Flexible cords shall be connected to devices and fittings so that strain relief is provided which will prevent pull from being directly transmitted to joints or terminal screws."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.405, Wiring methods, components, and equipment for general use (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which of these does 1926.405 list as a prohibited use of flexible cords and cables (unless needed for a permitted use)?

options.A: Pendants
options.B: As a substitute for the fixed wiring of a structure
options.C: Wiring of cranes and hoists
options.D: Connection of portable lamps or appliances

questions.explanation: Unless necessary for a permitted use, flexible cords and cables shall not be used "As a substitute for the fixed wiring of a structure." Pendants, crane and hoist wiring and portable lamps are on the permitted list.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.405, Wiring methods, components, and equipment for general use (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How must the entrances to rooms and other guarded locations containing exposed live parts be marked?

options.A: With the name of the electrician on duty
options.B: With yellow floor tape only
options.C: With conspicuous warning signs forbidding unqualified persons to enter
options.D: They need no marking if the door is kept closed

questions.explanation: "Entrances to rooms and other guarded locations containing exposed live parts shall be marked with conspicuous warning signs forbidding unqualified persons to enter."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.403, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For equipment at 600 volts or less with live parts likely to be serviced while alive, the working space in front of the equipment must be at least how wide?

options.A: 12 inches
options.B: 18 inches
options.C: 24 inches
options.D: 30 inches

questions.explanation: "In addition to the dimensions shown in Table K-1, workspace shall not be less than 30 inches (762 mm) wide in front of the electric equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.403, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where the exact location of underground electric powerlines is unknown, what must employees using jack-hammers, bars or other hand tools that may contact a line be provided with?

options.A: Insulated protective gloves
options.B: Hearing protection
options.C: High-visibility vests
options.D: Steel-toe boots

questions.explanation: Those employees "shall be provided with insulated protective gloves."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.416, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Before work begins, how must the employer find out whether an energized electric power circuit, exposed or concealed, is located where the work could bring a person, tool or machine into contact with it?

options.A: Only after work has begun, by checking any lines that are uncovered
options.B: By inquiry or direct observation, or by instruments
options.C: By assuming that any concealed circuit is deenergized
options.D: By having the building inspector sign off after the work is finished

questions.explanation: "Before work is begun the employer shall ascertain by inquiry or direct observation, or by instruments, whether any part of an energized electric power circuit, exposed or concealed, is so located" that the work may bring anyone or anything into contact with it.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.416, General requirements (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.417, what must the tags used on circuits and equipment identify?

options.A: The date of the last OSHA inspection
options.B: The employer's mailing address
options.C: Plainly, the equipment or circuits being worked on
options.D: The brand of the circuit breaker

questions.explanation: "Tags shall be placed to identify plainly the equipment or circuits being worked on."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.417, Lockout and tagging of circuits (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: As Subpart K applies the term to live parts, what does "exposed" mean?

options.A: Visible from a distance
options.B: Operating at more than 600 volts
options.C: Located outdoors
options.D: Capable of being inadvertently touched or approached nearer than a safe distance by a person

questions.explanation: Exposed (as applied to live parts) means "Capable of being inadvertently touched or approached nearer than a safe distance by a person. It is applied to parts not suitably guarded, isolated, or insulated."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.449, Definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)
